Tatjana Schoenmaker Olympics

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tatjana Shoenmaker, the latest Breaststroke Diamond out of South Africa

Summary:
Tatjana’s swim to Gold in the 200m breaststroke in Tokyo’s 2020 Olympics was called a standout performance by sports commentators. Swimming alongside her swimming compatriot Kaylene Corbett, Tatjana set a new world record. History has been made in Tokyo, the first individual swimming world record to be broken at this year’s games.

Watched from the stands by double Olympic gold medallist Penny Heyns, Tatjana burst into tears when she looked up at the screen and suddenly realised she had beaten the world record. It could not have been better scripted. Emotional scenes followed as the two South Africans and American swimmers, silver medallist, Lilly King and bronze winner Annie Lazor hugged each other with beaming smiles for all to see.



Further information:
Its been a long journey for 24 year-old Tatjana who began swimming at age five and competing at eight year’s old. When she won the 25 m butterfly, “ my parents decided that swimming was for me”

A profile on Tajana’s road to gold, talking to her parents Renske and Rene, her sister Fabienne, they are a close and supportive family and were overwhelmed after the swim as Tatjana spoke to them on the poolside family feed.

Her coach Rocco Meiring, from Tuks Sport in Pretoria, has been very much part of her success and nearly wasn’t in Tokyo after being struck down with Covid and very nearly dying. Rocco believes that Tatjana will be one of the world’s greatest swimmers.

Tatjana is committed to her charity ‘ Precious Blessings’ a care home for abused and abandoned babies and toddlers. She is very vocal on focusing on the youth of South Africa, inspiring and making their lives better not only with the swimmers but with the community.

She wasn’t even born when Penny Heyns, her lifelong swimming idol, won double gold in 1996. ‘Heyns was trailblazer of her time and remains among the greats as the only woman in history to win both the 100m and 200m breaststroke gold medals’. Tatjana is now following in Heyn’s footsteps and re-energising South African female swimming with their first swimming medal since the 2000 Olympics.

She nearly gave up after narrowly failing to qualify for the Rio Olympics in 2016 (by less than half a second) but followed her own advice to take the knocks, get up again and have the mental strength to refocus and keep going.

Advice that saw her early Friday morning -SA time- on the Olympic podium, in tears, as she is presented one of the rare gold medals and a bouquet by veteran South African Olympic official Sam Ramsammy.

Script:


Tatjana

Derek There is an image that brightened our lives that’s the final 200 metres  and your expression… 

Tatjana Schoenmaker

Tatjana: In my head I knew I wasn’t swimming best time but could still try and win the race then the last 50 metres I was just like I am just going to give it and as   touched I didn’t even look at the board yet //// So then I already  knew I won but first time I turned around and no one saw any reaction I saw a time 2 19 and thought that’s good I m on my time I looked and saw Kayleen was 5th and thought thank goodness we are done with the race and then I looked back  and saw 2. 19  wasn’t my time  and that’s when the whole reaction came
 
V/O 6 sec
Her time of  2 minutes 18.95 seconds a world record.
 
Link:Tatyana's exuberance says it all. This was a dream moment. But it nearly didn't happen...all because of a massive disappointment before the Rio Olympics in 2016
 
Rocco: That nearly broke her.  The fact that she swam the qualifying time prior to trials and then missed by 0.1 sec absolutely heartbreaking ,
 
Rocco Meiring
TuksSwimming- Head of Programmes

V/O 6 sec
For Rocco Meiring Tatjana’s coach these are the times that can break or make a champion

Tatjana: He was very calm in that and we knew it would be quiet a process as soon as I started getting back in pool though lets just try again.
 
Rocco: She was disillusioned she was first year 19 years old everybody was partying enjoying her life initially it was hard to get her to commit again but you know once they taste that success they are hooked *
  
V/O
Rocco first started coaching Tatjana when she was a schoolgirl.
 
Rocco: I have always seen in her that she is a fearless racer and when she came to me as a 14 year old  I knew I  had talent.
 
Tatjana: My parents knew swimming was my better sport in school
Derek:  Are they good swimmers
Tatjana:   No no one swam in my family I think when Rocco saw me at one competition at that point I didn’t like it that much to give my whole life to swimming I was a 14 year old trying to say I would rather play netball and they said I had talent in swimming I think they were right
 
Rocco: Apart from having great coach what are the ingredients a swimmer needs?
They need  very supportive and patient parents. Tatjana’s lucky  that she’s a product of her upbringing and you know true pressure comes out when pressures at its  highest/ the second thing they need that tenacity and determination to do the work.  

V/O 9 sec
After the disappointment of Rio, Tatjana went on to win two golds in 2018  in the Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast, Australia.
 
Tatjana: That was  also a funny story  because I actually asked Rocco if it was maybe possible to come third and get a sponsor or something because I saw Acani driving his Mercedes and I thought maybe it was possible to just get a sponsor and hoping to get a bronze coming from 7 to 6 but I never ever expected to walk out there with two gold medals.
Derek: You bagged the double 100 and 200
Tatjana : That was crazy thinking I had asked if possible just to get a bronze.
 
Theo: Everything she has achieved is very much in terms of her steely determination.

V/O
Sports Psychologist Theo Bezuidenhout joined  Tatjana’s team a year ago

Theo: I don’t think you can become elite if  you don’t acknowledge your weaknesses but also acknowledge your strengths and I've got to give her full credit there she is a person who works on her  strengths but recognize weaknesses and adjust to them.
  
Link: Amidst the tragedy of the pandemic, sports stars have also seen their lives change...and the postponement of the Tokyo Olympics meant that many athletes had to realign their goals 
 
Rocco: She handled it much better than I did. Its no secret dep religious approach to life and in her mind it was beyond her control . I was the one going off my head and she said to me don’t worry we’’ pick things up when the swimming pools open up again
 
Tatjana:  2016 to 2020 those years flew by and in Jan 6 months to go before Covid happened and I thought so rushed and felt if I had only one more year  so that  year a blessing what I needed  biggest goal about to come true…

Link: Much of the talk over the past few months has been over the mental pressures at the top level of sport....from young tennis stars to legends of gymnastics...and swimming is no exception
 
Theo: Social media has brought in immense pressure on athletes and always having to cover your wickets from that negative impact also trying to leverage positive side of social media with income and sponsorship. So something that we also  game planned and she did is I don’t think you would have been able to reach Tat on any social media platform for up to 3 months out of Tokyo which I think helped a lot because you could also quiet the noise as a tea.
 
V/O 7 sec
What Tatjana has been very vocal on social media about is her charity Precious Blessings a home for abused and abandoned babies.
 
Tatiana: They are such amazing people  what they do and the things they do for those children spending time with those children are so special and you just whish they could get those amazing families that would just love them.

V/O 5 sec
Heidi and George Versveld opened their home and hearts nine years ago.
 
Heidi: It’s not a publicity thing for her. For her it’s all about spending time with the children, playing with them, reading to them. It’s more like a friend coming to visit.
 
Derek : Just seen the pic what was it like performing without crowds?
Tatjana: it was different but my first Olympics. Having 20 00 people in crowds would have been been different but made us more calm wasn’t that extreme… food insane ..so for any athlete hard  to go to village dining hall maintain what you eat because now you have to carry on eating your eggs oats when you have French Toast waffles …how do you not want to eat that  Us swimmers we were always like when we see something last day.
 
V/O 
In the UK each Olympic  swimmer had 14 millions rands worth of funding a very different situation in South Africa.  
 
Derek: Rocco overseas millions are put behind athletes, we don’t have that money is it a big factor?big
Rocco: It is a very big factor. I have learned a long time ago you have got to do with what and you have got to cut through the really essential things. The fact that there's no money hinders us in terms of international preparation which is very important we cant go on training camps because there is no money/ but so far we have to Africanised approach and I often look at the Kenyan athletes its an inspiration They have nothing so If I compare that I have no excuses.  
 
 V/O 
In the 100 metre heats Tatjana broke an Olympic record…. Then in the finals she won a silver, three days later Rocco watched from poolside, the 200 metre breastroke
 
Rocco: I felt like a pilot flying a broken plane in bad weather it’s the most nerve wracking helpless experience because you cant coach that you cant coach that winning in a swimmer. I am very lucky to have her because she has got great instinct
 
Derek: First time for a while we have had 2 women swimmers in a final
Tatjana: It was very special because there was doubles, Great Britain Double US and doubles us and we were training partners so Kayleen and I trained together at Tuks.so it was so amazing to have that person in the pool.
 
V/O 
Tatjana’s prize moment was the support she got from fellow swimmers immediately after her win

Tatjana: For me hat was the best moment of the Olympics to share that moment with the girls…
Derek: When its all over time for a group hug
Tatjana: Or a group photo
